summary: A card for a shoulder armour you cut out yourself: fourteen flat panels off one A2 sheet, locked with tabs, no glue. Nobody has cut one yet, so the page it opens is where that lands.
license_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 covers this card's design and artwork — the panel geometry, the 1:1 sheet, and both card faces. It is what the page declares in its #vc-card block and repeats in its Licence section, and it is NOT the repository's MIT. The full legal code ships beside the package as examples/manis-card/LICENSE: Creative Commons' published text for CC BY-NC 4.0, 19,347 bytes, sha256 41003d4a74749c0220e33dd415042164b5a1093ed401f36277234f772d22d3d0 — re-fetched from creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/legalcode.txt on 2026-08-17 and byte-identical under cmp, which is the check NOTICE claims and this run repeated rather than trusted. NOTICE at the repo root, served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt, withholds ten of this card's files from the MIT grant — src/site/manis/card-{front,back}.png, src/web/cards/manis-{front,back}.png, the four PNGs in examples/manis-card/designs/, and examples/manis-card/assets/{front_editorial,back_blueprint}.png — and explicitly does not withhold the generated 645x645 qr_fallback.png in that same assets directory. Nothing in this manifest enlarges that withholding, and NOTICE grants nothing: it only ever takes away. Replication, as the #vc-card block declares it, is "noncommercial": print this card, cut the design, remix it, teach with it — credit it and do not sell it. The vibe-cards code around the card stays MIT.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /manis/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards (GitHub's repo API, anonymous, reports fork=false, private=false, created 2026-08-10T04:18:51Z), published on that repo's Pages surface. Its MIT is the host repo's, inherited by the code around the card and not chosen for the design — which is why the design carries its own licence file instead. THE CARD DID NOT ORIGINATE HERE. The object, the 1:1 blueprint, the editorial render and the four-colour palette arrived as a finished package from another system, named in the package's own machine-readable provenance — examples/manis-card/tools/build_card.py:271, written into the #vc-card block of examples/manis-card/package/index.html: inherited_from "REPLICABLE_NOVEL_VIBE_CARD (KIKKO CRAFTWORKS, run PB-47-92-12) — object, blueprint, editorial render and palette. The composition, geometry and wish route are rebuilt here." The commit that brought it in says the same and says why only the assets survived: f646571, 2026-08-15 13:16:58 -0700, author Agent-1 <agent@resonance.ai>, "The arriving composition was rendered before it was trusted: its kicker ran under the photo, the photo was clipped by the face edge, the blueprint sat illegible in a 16 mm circle, and the back printed the card's own build log... Assets kept, composition rebuilt." The front figure is a synthetic render from an image model (run PB-47-92-12), declared on the page a stranger reads rather than only in metadata, and it depicts no real person. WHO OR WHAT OPERATED THAT RUN IS NOT RECORDED IN THIS REPOSITORY, and this manifest does not know: grep for KIKKO or REPLICABLE_NOVEL across every tracked .py/.md/.json/.html/.mjs returns FIVE tracked files, measured 2026-08-17 with `git grep -lIE 'KIKKO|REPLICABLE_NOVEL' -- '*.py' '*.md' '*.json' '*.html' '*.mjs'`: this package's build script and built page, and three files under examples/aurelia-card/docs/ (ITINERARY.md, AUTONOMOUS_HIERARCHY_LOG.md and README.md). This sentence said four and named four until the count was re-run rather than inherited — the missed file is aurelia's README, and the correction is recorded here rather than quietly applied because a miscount in the paragraph that concludes 'authorship is unrecorded' is the paragraph least entitled to one that list PB-47-92-12 as a banned-for-reuse template lineage — and none of them names a model, a person, or any terms attached to that run. The CC BY-NC grant above therefore rests on NOTICE's assertion that this material "IS this project's to grant", which this file carries forward and did not independently verify. Downstream, unverified: examples/kaze-card/docs/README.md:40 lists "tab-and-slot solver from MANIS-CUIRASS-001" as an entry fee, and no such solver exists in this package — grep -rina solver over examples/manis-card returns nothing. The tab geometry lives in the blueprint raster and in the numbers printed on the card, not in code.
_note:
A PAGE-PROJECT'S MANIFEST, AT THE PAGE'S OWN URL. Criterion 4 reads "its repo root, or its listed url for a page-project", and the gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json, so this repo publishes several: the root declares L1 for the seed, /gt/ declares L0 for that page, and this file declares L0 for this card. Hand-authored and committed BEFORE any listing, deliberately. tools/build_site.py can derive a manifest, but only for entries already in listed[], so a derived one would be produced by the act of listing and criterion 4 would be satisfying itself. The builder's authored arm keeps a tracked file rather than overwriting it and checks one thing about it — that its level equals the registry badge — so whichever badge this card is given must read L0 or the build fails.

WHY L0. All three clauses are measured on the deployed surface, not the working tree, because the working tree is exactly what fooled the last two promotions: AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 sat held on criterion 4 while the manifest existed uncommitted. Measured 2026-08-17, anonymous curl, control path on the same host 404 every time. (1) "This file present": WISH_IT_BETTER.md is at the repo root and served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md, 200. (2) "A wish channel that works": the well is on THIS page, not the landing page — https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/manis/ returns 200 (30,721 bytes, last-modified Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:32:21 GMT) and those served bytes carry exactly one data-wish-well marker, on a button beside a textarea that POSTs to a public insert-only Supabase queue, with "No account, no email, nothing to sign up for" printed under it. Declared without a fragment on purpose: this page has no id="wish" anchor (0 occurrences), so #wish would point at nothing. (3) "A LICENSE": GitHub's licence API returns spdx_id MIT for the repo root anonymously, and this card's own CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code sits beside the package.

WHY NOT L1, on both of its clauses. (a) "Every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2": docs/EVALS.md, the file this manifest points at, contains 0 occurrences of manis, cuirass or compound craft in 147 lines — it is Card Studio's eval record, the tool that printed the card, not this card's. Changes to this card do carry numbers, but in commit messages (f646571: "Faces measured at 2066x1319, QR decoded from both shipped copies"), and a commit message is not the record §2 asks for. E2 is unmet at the deepest point: NOBODY HAS CUT THIS MANTLE. src/site/manis/entries.json says so in its own _doc — "nothing here was measured off a built object, because nobody has built one" — so the 12.0 mm tab, the 12.4 mm slot and the 0.6 m² are drawing arithmetic, not a fit anyone has felt. (b) "Wishes reach a terminal state": tools/wishing_well.py implements new -> building -> shipped/declined and refuses --decline without a reason, so the machinery is real, but whether any wish about THIS card ever reached a terminal state cannot be read from here. The page's anon key is insert-only; a GET with it returns 200 [] while a nonsense table on the same project returns 404 PGRST205, which proves the endpoint and key are live and proves nothing about the queue — an empty array under row-level security is what a blocked read looks like. Unverified is not satisfied. The two entries in the page's log are corrections this project wrote, not wishes it shipped. If in doubt §3 says L0, and the spec's own v1.0.1 amendment earns nobody L2.

WHAT THE FIELDS CANNOT CARRY. THE CHIP IS UNWRITTEN. network.json's card ledger records surface "chip" for manis-card as url null: "No tag has been programmed for this card yet." The url in this manifest is real and live, but today it reaches a holder through the QR printed on the card's back face, not through a chip. That QR was decoded from two shipped artifacts — examples/manis-card/designs/back_85.6x53.98mm_600dpi.png and src/web/cards/manis-back.png, both to https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/manis/ — by the run that wrote the ledger entry, using ./tools/qrdecode; this pass read that record and did not re-decode the rasters. The package has no README and no docs/: assets, designs, LICENSE, package, tools, and that is all, so a reader who wants the build steps reads the page, not the package. The deployed page and the tracked source agree this run — src/site/manis/card-front.png is byte-identical to what Pages serves, sha256 1e68c5e3801ce3e8c87e21477d14292126423a6a0877ff990545c29f400357b5, and git status is clean for every manis path at HEAD 47ba30c. Two grants sit over one tree on purpose; if this file and NOTICE ever disagree, NOTICE is the one that withholds and this one is wrong.
